card: PR #35037 adds per-listener connection limiting to `-ipcbind` via inline options (e.g., `-ipcbind=unix:/path.sock,max-connections=8`), defaulting to 16 and capped at 256. It incorporates IPC listener sockets and connection limits into startup file descriptor reservation, preventing unconstrained IPC connections from causing file descriptor exhaustion. It serves as an alternative to the global limit proposed in PR #34978, enabling distinct connection limits for different IPC endpoints.
changed_since_previous: Added URL decoding for Unix socket paths to allow commas encoded as %2C, updated parser test coverage for encoded paths, and documented URL decoding in the release notes.
evidence: PR description: 'This keeps the connection limit attached to each IPC listener instead of introducing a global -ipcmaxconnections option (pull #34978). A global option would not allow different limits for different -ipcbind addresses...'

Commit 3d2b65d050: 'Reserve file descriptors for each configured -ipcbind listener and its default connection slots during initialization. Cap IPC reservations conservatively so downstream int-based file descriptor accounting cannot overflow.'
problem: IPC listening sockets previously lacked connection limits and were omitted from startup file descriptor reservation checks, risking file descriptor exhaustion and node instability under heavy IPC socket usage. Additionally, a single global `-ipcmaxconnections` setting cannot support different connection limits across distinct IPC listeners.

risk.why: A parsing or accounting bug in init could prevent node startup when -ipcbind is configured.

summary: Extends `-ipcbind` to accept per-listener `,max-connections=<n>` socket options (defaulting to 16, capped at 256) and URL-decodes Unix socket paths to allow commas in file paths. Incorporates IPC listening sockets and connection limits into node initialization file descriptor accounting and reservation. Forwards the per-listener limits through `interfaces::Ipc` to enforce connection caps on incoming IPC sockets.
